title: Take the Mic
prompt: Find an open mic this week. Sign up. Perform anything for three minutes: a poem, a song, a passage from a book you love. Your hands may shake. Do it anyway.
why: Nothing rewires your fear thermostat like being seen on purpose.
easier: Go to an open mic as an audience member and talk to one performer afterwards.

title: Bus to Nowhere
prompt: Get on the first bus that arrives at the nearest stop. Ride it for at least eight stops, get off, and find one thing worth photographing before you head home.
why: Your city is mostly unexplored. You just keep taking the same lines.
easier: Take a bus you know, but get off three stops early and walk the rest.
safety: Check how you'll get back before you go. Tell someone where you're headed.

title: The Best Advice
prompt: Ask a stranger over 60: "What's the best advice anyone ever gave you?" Listen to the whole answer. Write it down word for word afterwards.
why: Elders are libraries nobody visits.
easier: Ask a relative or neighbour over 60 the same question.

title: Public Sweat
prompt: Do a full 30-minute bodyweight workout in a public park. Push-ups, squats, lunges, planks. No headphones for the last ten minutes.
why: Self-consciousness is a muscle too. Train it to shut up.
easier: Do the workout at home with the window wide open.

title: Public Reading
prompt: Stand in a park, square or plaza and read one page of a book you love out loud, at a volume someone ten metres away could hear.
why: Voices get small when they're never used at full size.
easier: Record yourself reading the page and send it to a friend.

title: The Precise Compliment
prompt: Give a stranger a compliment so specific it could only be about them. Not "nice shoes": "that green with that coat is a genuinely brave choice and it works."
why: Specific praise proves you actually looked. That's rare and it lands.
easier: Send a hyper-specific compliment to someone you haven't spoken to in a year.

title: Catch the Sunrise
prompt: Set an alarm, get outside, and watch the sun come up from the highest point you can reach on foot. No phone until it's fully up, except for one photo.
why: Most people see a few dozen sunrises in their whole life. Raise your number.
easier: Watch the sunrise from your window with a hot drink and no phone.

title: Ninety Cold Seconds
prompt: End your shower with 90 seconds of fully cold water. Breathe slowly through your nose. Don't flinch out early.
why: Choosing discomfort on purpose makes unchosen discomfort feel smaller.
easier: Thirty seconds, cold on arms and legs only.
safety: Skip this if you have a heart condition.

title: Table for One
prompt: Eat dinner alone at a sit-down restaurant. No phone, no book. Just the food, the room, and your own company.
why: If you can't enjoy your own company, nobody else's will be enough.
easier: Coffee alone at a café, no phone, for twenty minutes.

title: Ink and Stamp
prompt: Hand-write a real letter to someone who shaped you and post it. Tell them one specific moment they probably don't know mattered.
why: A letter is a physical object of love. It ends up in drawers for decades.
easier: Write a long, careful voice note instead.

title: Karaoke Kamikaze
prompt: Go to a karaoke bar and sing a song in front of strangers. Commit to the whole song, including the bit you don't know.
why: The audience is rooting for you more than you think. Find out.
easier: Private karaoke room with two friends, and you pick the first song.

title: Regular Status
prompt: Learn the name of someone who serves you regularly (barista, cashier, bus driver) and use it next time you see them.
why: Cities feel lonely until you name the faces in them.
easier: Thank them and make eye contact for a full second.

title: Uncharted 10k
prompt: Walk 10,000 steps without repeating a single street. No map for the first half, just turn wherever looks interesting.
why: Getting a little lost is how places become yours.
easier: 5,000 steps in a neighbourhood you've never walked.
safety: Keep your phone charged for the way back.

title: Portrait of a Stranger
prompt: Ask a stranger if you can take their portrait. Tell them honestly why they caught your eye. Offer to send them the photo.
why: Asking for something small with no excuse is a superpower in disguise.
easier: Ask a street performer or vendor, who is used to being noticed.

title: Analog Day
prompt: Put your phone in a drawer from waking until 6pm. Tell the people who need to know. Notice every time your hand reaches for it.
why: You'll learn exactly how much of your day is reflex.
easier: Phone-free from waking until noon.

title: Foreign Kitchen
prompt: Cook a dish from a cuisine you have never cooked before, using one ingredient you've never bought. Serve it to someone, or plate it like it's for a critic.
why: Competence in new territory is the fastest confidence there is.
easier: Make one new sauce and put it on something familiar.

title: Just Ask
prompt: Ask for a discount somewhere that doesn't normally give one. Smile, be polite, and expect a no. Collect the no like a trophy.
why: Rejection is survivable. Learn it in a place where the stakes are a coffee.
easier: Ask a café to put a funny name on your cup.

title: Plank Personal Best
prompt: Hold a plank as long as you possibly can. Write down the time. Then rest two minutes and beat it by five seconds.
why: Your 'limit' is usually just the first time it gets uncomfortable.
easier: Plank on your knees, same rules.

title: One Painting, Twenty Minutes
prompt: Go to a museum or gallery and look at a single piece for twenty uninterrupted minutes. Then write three things you noticed only after minute ten.
why: Attention is the rarest thing you own. Spend it lavishly once.
easier: Ten minutes with one tree, building or photo.

title: Yes Day
prompt: For one day, say yes to every reasonable invitation, suggestion or offer, no matter how small. Track what you'd normally have refused.
why: Your default 'no' is quietly editing your life.
easier: Say yes to the next three invitations.
safety: "Reasonable" is doing real work here. Safety and money still count.

title: Wild Swim
prompt: Swim in a lake, river or sea, somewhere that isn't a pool. Get your head under at least once.
why: Cold open water makes you feel more alive than almost anything legal.
easier: Wade in up to your waist and stay for two minutes.
safety: Only swim in known safe spots, never alone, and be honest with yourself about cold water.

title: Find Your Teacher
prompt: Track down a teacher, coach or mentor from your past and message them: what they taught you, and where it shows up in your life now.
why: Teachers almost never hear how the story ends.
easier: Write the message even if you can't find them, and keep it.

title: Chalk Message
prompt: Write a short, kind message in chalk on a pavement where people will walk past. Something you'd want to read on a bad day.
why: Anonymous kindness is the purest kind: no credit, all effect.
easier: Leave a kind note in a library book.
safety: Use washable chalk and public pavement only.

title: Ask a Local
prompt: Ask a shop owner where they personally eat lunch. Go there. Order what they told you to order.
why: The best map of a city lives in its people, not its apps.
easier: Ask a coworker or neighbour for their favourite hidden spot and go.

title: Kitchen Rave
prompt: Put on the most ridiculous song you secretly love and dance to the entire thing like nobody will ever know. Full body. Arms included.
why: Joy without an audience is the original kind.
easier: Dance for one chorus only.

title: Beginner Again
prompt: Book a single drop-in class in something you've never tried: pottery, salsa, climbing, life drawing, improv. Be the worst person in the room on purpose.
why: Being a beginner is the fastest way to feel young again.
easier: Follow a full-length beginner tutorial for something new at home.

title: Trade a Recommendation
prompt: In a bookshop or record store, ask a stranger what they'd recommend, then recommend them something back. Buy (or note down) theirs.
why: Taste shared with a stranger is a tiny act of trust.
easier: Ask the staff member for their personal favourite.

title: Night Walk
prompt: Take a slow walk after dark through a part of your neighbourhood you only know in daylight. Notice the sounds, the lit windows, the smells.
why: The same streets become a different world after sunset.
easier: Walk around the block at dusk with no headphones.
safety: Stick to well-lit areas you'd be comfortable in. Tell someone.

title: A Poem in an Hour
prompt: Write a poem about something you saw today. Not about feelings in general, about one thing you saw. Read it aloud to yourself once when it's done.
why: Writing a poem forces you to actually notice your own day.
easier: Write a haiku about the view from your window.

title: Call, Don't Text
prompt: Phone a friend you'd normally only text. No reason needed. If they ask why, say: "I wanted to hear your voice."
why: Voices carry what text can't. People remember calls.
easier: Send a voice message instead of a text.

title: Summit Something
prompt: Climb to the top of the nearest hill, peak or tall natural point you can reach on foot. Eat something at the top.
why: Views you earned taste better. Sandwiches too.
easier: Climb every flight of stairs in the tallest public building you can access.
safety: Check weather, bring water, tell someone your route.

title: Pay It Forward
prompt: Pay for the coffee, bus fare or groceries of the person behind you. If they ask, just say "pass it on."
why: A small surprise kindness can redirect someone's whole day.
easier: Leave an unusually generous tip with a thank-you note.

title: Hour of Silence
prompt: Sit or walk for one hour with no input at all: no music, podcast, phone, book or conversation. Just your thoughts.
why: You can't hear yourself if you're never quiet.
easier: Fifteen minutes, sitting outside.

title: Ask the Way
prompt: Ask a stranger for directions to somewhere nearby, even though your phone knows. Then ask them their favourite thing about the area.
why: It's the gentlest possible way to start talking to strangers again.
easier: Ask someone for the time.

title: Show Up for Someone
prompt: Volunteer for one shift: a food bank, an animal shelter, a park clean-up, a soup kitchen. Talk to at least one other volunteer.
why: Being useful to strangers is one of the most reliable sources of meaning.
easier: Do a solo litter pick on your street for thirty minutes.

title: Ticket Lottery
prompt: Go to the train station, pick a town within two hours you've never heard of, and spend the day there. Find the best thing to eat in it.
why: Small unknown places are where travel stories come from.
easier: Spend half a day in a neighbourhood across town you've never visited.
safety: Check return times before you leave.

title: Full Volume
prompt: Sing one song at full volume, with feeling. Neighbours be damned. Bonus if the window is open.
why: Most adults haven't sung at full volume in years. Your lungs miss it.
easier: Sing in the car with the windows up.

title: First 5k
prompt: Run 5 kilometres. Walk when you need to, but cover the whole distance. Note your time without judging it.
why: Distance is democratic. Anyone who keeps moving finishes.
easier: Run/walk 2 kilometres.
safety: Go at your own pace, especially if you're new to running.

title: Their Language
prompt: Learn a full sentence in the native language of someone you see regularly (a shopkeeper, neighbour, colleague) and say it to them.
why: Effort in someone's language is a form of respect they never forget.
easier: Learn "thank you" and "have a good day" and use them.

title: Letter to Future You
prompt: Write a letter to yourself, to be opened exactly one year from today. Ask yourself three questions. Seal it and set a reminder.
why: Future you deserves a message from the person you are right now.
easier: Write one paragraph and email it to yourself on a delay.

title: The Seatmate
prompt: Start a real conversation with the person next to you on a train, bus, plane or bench. Find out one thing about them that surprises you.
why: Studies keep finding we enjoy talking to strangers far more than we predict.
easier: Comment on something you both can see and see where it goes.
safety: Read the room. Headphones in means not today.

title: Upside Down
prompt: Learn to hold a handstand against a wall for 20 seconds. Film the attempt where you finally get it.
why: Seeing the world upside down is genuinely good for the brain.
easier: Hold a headstand-prep or downward dog for one minute.
safety: Clear space, soft floor, and skip this if you have neck or wrist issues.

title: Thrift Store Persona
prompt: Buy a complete outfit from a second-hand shop that someone with a completely different life would wear. Wear it out for an hour.
why: Clothes are costumes. Try a different character on for a bit.
easier: Buy one bold thrifted item and wear it today.

title: Find Three Constellations
prompt: Get somewhere dark, let your eyes adjust for 15 minutes, and find three constellations without using an app until you've tried.
why: The sky is the oldest show in town and it's free every night.
easier: Find the Moon and one bright planet tonight.
safety: Choose a safe dark spot, ideally with someone.

title: Overdue Apology
prompt: Apologise for something you've been avoiding. No excuses, no "but". Just what you did, that you're sorry, and what you'd do differently.
why: Unfinished apologies take up space in your head for years.
easier: Write the apology fully, then decide in 24 hours whether to send it.

title: Café Sketch
prompt: Sit in a café and draw the room, people included. If someone notices, show them. Badness is not only allowed, it's encouraged.
why: Drawing forces you to see, not just look.
easier: Draw your own hand for ten minutes.

title: Two Wheels, New Route
prompt: Rent or borrow a bike and ride to a place you'd normally reach by car or transit. Take the scenic way, not the fast one.
why: Cycling shows you the connective tissue of a city.
easier: A 20-minute ride around a park.
safety: Helmet, lights, and quiet roads.

title: Twenty Still Minutes
prompt: Sit still for twenty minutes and count your breaths from one to ten, then start again. Every time you lose count, start at one without judgement.
why: Your attention can be trained. This is the gym.
easier: Five minutes, same rules.

title: Knock with Food
prompt: Bake or cook something and give some to a neighbour you barely know. Introduce yourself properly.
why: Neighbourhoods are built one plate at a time.
easier: Leave a small treat and a note at their door.

title: Five Minutes of Funny
prompt: Write five minutes of stand-up about your own life and perform it at a comedy open mic. Bombing counts as completing the challenge.
why: If you survive bombing in front of strangers, very little will scare you again.
easier: Perform your set to three friends, standing up, with a fake mic.

title: Ask for the Truth
prompt: Ask someone who knows you well: "What's one thing I do that holds me back?" Thank them. Don't defend yourself.
why: Everyone around you can see your blind spot. Borrow their eyes.
easier: Ask for one thing you're doing well and one to try differently, in writing.

title: Lane Lines
prompt: Go to a public pool and swim 20 lengths without stopping at either end. Any stroke counts.
why: Rhythmic breathing in water is moving meditation.
easier: Swim 10 lengths, rest as needed.

title: The Big Question
prompt: At your next meal with others, ask: "What's something you changed your mind about recently?" Don't let anyone dodge, yourself included.
why: One good question turns small talk into a conversation people remember.
easier: Ask one friend the question by message.

title: Twenty Photos of Red
prompt: Go for a walk and take 20 photos of one colour or shape. You'll start seeing it everywhere. Pick the best one as your card photo.
why: Constraints make the familiar strange again.
easier: Ten photos, inside your home.

title: Put Roots Down
prompt: Plant something that will outlive this week: a herb on your windowsill, a bulb in a shared garden, a tree if you can. Give it a name.
why: Caring for something slow is an antidote to a fast life.
easier: Regrow a spring onion from its root in a glass of water.

title: Busk for a Coin
prompt: Perform in public for 20 minutes with a hat or case open: an instrument, singing, juggling, poetry, anything. Earn at least one coin.
why: Getting paid by a stranger for art is a feeling you never forget.
easier: Play or sing for ten minutes on a bench without a hat.
safety: Check whether busking needs a permit where you live.

title: Walk and Talk
prompt: Turn a call or meeting into a walking one. If it's in person, propose the walk instead of sitting down.
why: Side-by-side conversations are more honest than face-to-face ones.
easier: Take your next phone call while walking outside.

title: Complaint Fast
prompt: Go a full day without complaining out loud, about anything. Each time you slip, note it and restart the clock.
why: You'll discover how much complaining is just social filler.
easier: Half a day, and only count complaints about other people.

title: Fifty Push-ups
prompt: Do 50 push-ups today in as few sets as possible. Knees are allowed after your first set fails.
why: A big round number is a satisfying wall to climb.
easier: 25 push-ups, any style.

title: Release a Book
prompt: Leave a book you loved somewhere public (a bench, a train, a café) with a note inside saying why it mattered to you.
why: Somewhere a stranger is about to have a very good day.
easier: Donate a book to a little free library.

title: Order the Weird Thing
prompt: Go to a restaurant serving food you know nothing about and order the dish you can't pronounce. Ask the staff to tell you its story.
why: Taste is a passport you can use without leaving town.
easier: Buy one fruit or snack you've never tried from a world grocery shop.
safety: Mention allergies to the staff.

title: The Clean No
prompt: Say no to something you don't want to do, without inventing an excuse. "No thank you, I'd rather not" is a complete sentence.
why: Every reluctant yes is time borrowed from your own life.
easier: Decline something by message without explaining why.

title: Join a Pickup Game
prompt: Walk up to a pickup game (football, basketball, frisbee, volleyball) and ask if you can join. Play until the game ends.
why: Sport with strangers is instant community with built-in small talk.
easier: Join a free running club's group run.

title: Carry a Poem
prompt: Memorise a poem of at least 12 lines. Recite it to someone tonight without looking.
why: A memorised poem is something nobody can ever take from you.
easier: Memorise four lines and write them from memory.

title: Tourist at Home
prompt: Do the number-one tourist thing in your city that you've never done because you live here. Buy the postcard.
why: Locals are the last to see what's special about where they live.
easier: Visit the most famous view in your city and take the cliché photo.

title: Gratitude Visit
prompt: Write a 300-word letter of thanks to someone alive whom you never properly thanked. Then visit them and read it aloud, in person.
why: In positive psychology trials, this is among the strongest single happiness boosters ever measured.
easier: Read it to them over a video call.

title: Under the Sky
prompt: Spend a night sleeping outside: a campsite, a garden, a balcony. Watch the sky until you fall asleep.
why: Waking up with the birds resets something in you.
easier: Lie outside after dark for an hour with a blanket.
safety: Choose a legal, safe spot and check the weather.

title: Family Archaeology
prompt: Ask a parent, grandparent or aunt a question about their life before you existed that you've never asked. Record the answer if they let you.
why: These stories have an expiry date. Collect them now.
easier: Ask them about their first job.

title: No Elevators
prompt: Take the stairs every single time today. Escalators count as elevators. Count your flights.
why: Small choices, multiplied, are what a body is made of.
easier: Stairs for anything under four floors.

title: Make a Zine
prompt: Fold one sheet of paper into an eight-page mini zine about anything you care about. Photocopy it and leave three copies in public.
why: Publishing something, however tiny, makes you an author.
easier: Make one copy and give it to a friend.

title: The Origin Story
prompt: Ask the owner of an independent shop or restaurant how they started it. Let them tell the whole story.
why: Every small business is a bet someone made. People love telling theirs.
easier: Ask a staff member how long they've worked there and what's changed.

title: Delete Ten Apps
prompt: Delete ten apps from your phone. Move the remaining ones you overuse off your home screen.
why: Your home screen is a decision about what your life looks at.
easier: Delete three, and turn off notifications for five more.

title: Salute the Sun
prompt: Do ten slow sun salutations outside first thing in the morning, barefoot if you can.
why: Starting the day in your body instead of your inbox changes its whole tone.
easier: Three sun salutations by an open window.

title: Thank the Invisible
prompt: Thank someone whose work is usually invisible (a cleaner, a bin collector, a night guard) with eye contact and a full sentence about what their work makes possible.
why: The people who keep the world running are thanked the least.
easier: Leave a thank-you note for your postal worker.

title: Forest Bathing
prompt: Spend one hour in a wood or large park walking very slowly. Touch five different textures. Find the oldest-looking tree and sit against it.
why: Time among trees measurably lowers stress. Your nervous system knows.
easier: Twenty minutes in the greenest place within walking distance.

title: Dance in Public
prompt: Go to a social dance night: salsa, swing, tango, ceilidh. Accept or ask for at least three dances.
why: Dancing with strangers is permission to be awkward together.
easier: Go and watch, and take the free beginner lesson at the start.

title: Glowing Review
prompt: Write a detailed, glowing review for a small local business that made your life better. Name the person who served you.
why: For small businesses a review is rent money. For staff it's a reason to stay.
easier: Tell the owner in person what you love about the place.

title: One-Hour Skill
prompt: Learn a party trick in one hour: juggling three balls, a card trick, whistling with fingers, solving one face of a Rubik's cube. Then show someone.
why: Small mastery is addictive in the best way.
easier: Learn to tie three new knots.

title: The Long Hug
prompt: Give someone you love a hug that lasts at least twenty seconds. Don't be the first to let go.
why: Long hugs release oxytocin. Short ones are just a greeting.
easier: Ten seconds. Still count it in your head.

title: Draw the Skyline
prompt: Find a high spot and draw the skyline in one continuous line without lifting the pen.
why: Drawing a place is how you really memorise it.
easier: Draw the view from your window in continuous line.

title: Invert Your Routine
prompt: Do your morning routine in reverse order, take a different route to work, and eat lunch somewhere new. Notice how alert you feel.
why: Autopilot is comfortable and forgettable. Novelty is how days become memories.
easier: Change just your route.

title: Join the Table
prompt: In a café, bar or communal space, ask a group or individual if you can join them. Explain honestly: you're doing a challenge to meet new people.
why: Most people are delighted by someone brave enough to be direct.
easier: Ask to share a table in a busy café and make one comment.
safety: Public places only, and leave gracefully if it isn't welcome.

title: Dawn Summit
prompt: Start a hike in the dark and reach a summit for sunrise. Pack something hot to drink at the top.
why: This is one of those mornings you'll remember when you're eighty.
easier: Reach a local viewpoint for sunrise.
safety: Headtorch, layers, a route you know, and never alone.

title: Birthday Song
prompt: Next birthday you know of: call and sing the entire happy birthday song. No text. Commit to the high note.
why: Embarrassing yourself a little for someone is a gift they keep.
easier: Send a recorded voice note of you singing.

title: Celebrate a Stranger
prompt: Go to a local race, game or event and cheer for strangers by name (from their bibs or shirts). Get at least one high five.
why: Cheering for people you'll never see again is joy in its purest form.
easier: Cheer loudly at a kids' match or local amateur game.

title: Free Up Something
prompt: Cancel one subscription you don't really use, and spend that month's money on an experience instead.
why: Turn passive spending into a memory.
easier: Look over all your subscriptions and write down what each costs per year.

title: Solo Show
prompt: Go to a concert, play or film screening alone. Talk to one person there about what you just saw.
why: Experiences hit harder when no one is managing your reaction.
easier: Go to a free gallery opening alone.

title: Make, Don't Buy
prompt: Make a gift for someone with your own hands: a candle, a mixtape, a drawing, a jam, a framed photo. Give it with no occasion.
why: An imperfect handmade thing outranks a perfect bought one, every time.
easier: Make a playlist for someone with a note for each song.

title: Barefoot Mile
prompt: Take off your shoes and walk barefoot on grass or sand for at least fifteen minutes. Notice every texture.
why: Your feet have 200,000 nerve endings and they spend all day in a box.
easier: Five minutes barefoot in a park.
safety: Check the ground for glass first.

title: First to Speak
prompt: In your next meeting, class or group conversation, be the first person to share an idea or opinion. Don't wait for it to be safe.
why: The first idea anchors the whole conversation. Be the anchor once.
easier: Ask the first question.

title: Note for a Stranger
prompt: Write five sticky notes with encouraging messages ("You're doing better than you think") and leave them on mirrors, ticket machines and lift buttons.
why: Someone having their worst day will find one. You'll never know who.
easier: Leave one note.

title: Ten Pairs of Hands
prompt: Photograph the hands of ten different strangers (with permission), each holding something that matters to them. Ask what it is.
why: Hands tell a life story. Asking to see them opens surprising doors.
easier: Photograph the hands of three people you know.

title: Get on the Water
prompt: Take any boat: a ferry, a rowing boat, a kayak, a pedalo. See your area from the water for the first time.
why: Water changes the angle. Everything looks new from it.
easier: Walk the full length of the nearest river or canal path.
safety: Life jackets on small craft.

title: New Sport
prompt: Try a sport you've never played: bouldering, fencing, archery, squash, roller skating. Book a beginner session.
why: New movement patterns grow new neural pathways. Also it's fun.
easier: Play a sport you haven't touched since school.

title: Say It Plainly
prompt: Tell someone, in person and in plain words, what they mean to you. Not a joke, not a hint. A friend counts.
why: The most common regret of the dying is not saying it.
easier: Write it in a message and send it before you can edit it.

title: Three Pages
prompt: Write three pages by hand, first thing in the morning, about anything. Don't stop the pen. Don't reread it.
why: Morning pages drain the mental noise so the real thoughts can come up.
easier: One page.

title: Leave It Better
prompt: Fill an entire bag with litter from a beach, park or street. Take a before-and-after photo.
why: Visible change you made with your own hands is deeply satisfying.
easier: Pick up ten pieces of litter on your walk.
safety: Use gloves and leave sharp objects to professionals.

title: Lift Talk
prompt: Start a conversation in a lift that lasts all the way to the other person's floor. Make them smile before the doors open.
why: The lift is the final boss of small talk. Beat it.
easier: Say good morning to everyone who gets in.

title: Midnight Swim
prompt: Swim in the sea or a lake at night with friends, under the moon. Float on your back and look up.
why: Some experiences are only available after dark and with a little nerve.
easier: Wade in at dusk with friends.
safety: Never alone, never drunk, only at a known calm spot.

title: Write a Song
prompt: Write a song: one verse and one chorus, even if it's just three chords or you sing it unaccompanied. Record it and send it to someone.
why: Everyone has a song in them. Most people die without hearing it.
easier: Write new lyrics to a song you love.

title: Sunrise to Sunset Fast
prompt: Eat nothing from sunrise to sunset; water is fine. Break the fast with a meal you cook slowly and eat slowly.
why: Hunger teaches gratitude faster than any book.
easier: Skip one meal and eat the next one mindfully.
safety: Skip this if pregnant, diabetic, or with any history of disordered eating.
